value_stream.name: Auto-ID, Barcode, RFID, Price-Tag Labeling & EAS Operations

fields.Trigger: Store open (VS-07.1); alarm; system health check
fields.Volume: EAS gates at all 200 store exits + deactivators at 600 POS

workflows.name: EAS System Operations (Gates, Deactivators, Exception Alerts)

Automation Opportunity: - EAS health/alarm dashboard; false-alarm-rate analytics; auto-sensitivity tuning guidance
Controls: - CTL-685 (ensure controlled execution — EAS/RFID Tagging, Source-Tagging & Loss-Prevention Integration (PA-151.3).)
- CTL-685: EAS daily-tested; sensitivity tuned; true alarms routed to response (W4501)
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP), VS-138 (IFM), VS-99 (ITAM), VS-08 (POS), W4485 (standard), W4501 (response)
Pain Points / Risks: - **False-alarm fatigue risk**: Over-sensitive gates → ignored real alarms; mitigated by sensitivity tuning & false-alarm tracking
- **Deactivator-failure risk**: Pad fails → legitimate exit alarms & customer friction; mitigated by daily function test
System Touchpoints: - LP/exception (VS-23); IFM maintenance (VS-138); ITAM (VS-99); POS deactivation (VS-08); service desk (VS-27.1)
Time Estimate: - ~15 min/day per store EAS ops; continuous monitoring

steps.activity: Stores/LP operate EAS gates/deactivators daily (power-up test, sensitivity check, deactivator-pad function), logging health per W4485 standard
IT/LP monitor EAS exception alerts (gate triggers), classify (true alarm vs false), and route true positives to LP response (W4501)
IFM/IT maintain EAS hardware (gate calibration/deactivator replacement) via VS-138/VS-99, tuning sensitivity to minimize false alarms while catching real events

fields.Trigger: Vendor contracting (VS-03); tagging-policy update (W4484); cost program

Automation Opportunity: - Source-tag coverage/ROI analytics; receipt auto-flag of untagged source-tag SKUs; vendor scorecard integration (VS-67)
Controls: - CTL-685 (ensure controlled execution — EAS/RFID Tagging, Source-Tagging & Loss-Prevention Integration (PA-151.3).)
- CTL-685: source-tag spec in contract; verified at receipt (VS-04); vendor compliance scored (VS-67)
Cross-references: - links to VS-03 (vendor), VS-04 (DC), VS-41 (private label), VS-23 (LP), VS-67 (scorecard), W4484 (tag policy), W4492 (in-store apply)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vendor-noncompliance risk**: Promised source-tags missing → in-store labor to apply; mitigated by receipt verification + vendor scorecard (VS-67)
- **Encoding-mismatch risk**: Vendor encodes wrong format; mitigated by spec-in-contract + receipt read-test
System Touchpoints: - Vendor mgmt (VS-03); DC receive (VS-04); private label (VS-41); LP/shrink (VS-23); W4484 tag policy
Time Estimate: - Per vendor ~2–4 weeks; ongoing receipt verification

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead/LP/Vendor Mgmt negotiate source-tagging agreements (vendor applies EAS/RFID at manufacture), selecting tag type/encoding per W4484 and reconciling cost (cheaper than in-store application)
DC/Auto-ID Lead verify source-tags at goods receipt (tag present, correct, read-able) per VS-04, flag missing tags for in-store application (W4492)
Private Label (VS-41) embeds source-tagging into own-brand production spec; Merchandising tracks source-tag coverage and ROI (W4503)

fields.Trigger: RFID program rollout; cycle-count (VS-05); real-time inventory (VS-60)

Automation Opportunity: - RFID-driven automated cycle-count; read-zone health/interference analytics; EPC auto-encoding
Controls: - CTL-685 (ensure controlled execution — EAS/RFID Tagging, Source-Tagging & Loss-Prevention Integration (PA-151.3).)
- CTL-685: RFID encoded to GS1 EPC (W4482); reads reconciled to inventory (VS-05); interference mitigated
Cross-references: - links to VS-05 (inventory/cycle-count), VS-04 (DC), VS-60 (omnichannel), VS-99 (ITAM), VS-23 (LP), W4482/W4484 (encoding/policy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Read-interference risk**: Metal/liquid SKUs (paint, cement, metal) degrade RFID reads; mitigated by tag-placement/reader-tuning & mixed-EAS fallback
- **Phantom-read risk**: Mis-placed tags create inventory ghosts; mitigated by read-zone validation & count reconciliation (VS-05)
System Touchpoints: - Inventory/cycle-count (VS-05); DC receive (VS-04); omnichannel visibility (VS-60); ITAM (VS-99); LP (VS-23); IFM (VS-138)
Time Estimate: - Per program weeks; ongoing ops integrated into cycle-count

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead/IT design/deploy RFID read-zones (DC portals, store handhelds, smart-shelf) per the W4484 policy, encode tags to the GS1 EPC standard (W4482), and integrate reads to inventory (VS-05/VS-60)
DC/Stores use RFID for cycle-counting (VS-05.1) and receiving (VS-04) — bulk scan vs line-by-line — improving count speed/accuracy toward the ≥97% target
IT/ITAM operate the RFID infrastructure (reader health, read-zone tuning, interference mgmt) via VS-99/VS-138, and feed exceptions (reads-outside-expected) to LP (VS-23)

fields.Trigger: Sale completion (VS-08); return (VS-32); tag pool replenishment
fields.Volume: Reusable hard-tags (EAS) cycled across high-value SKUs

Automation Opportunity: - POS-driven detach-confirmation; tag-pool count reconciliation app; shortage auto-alert to LP (VS-23)
Controls: - CTL-685: tags detached/deactivated at paid sale; reusable pool reconciled per shift; shortages investigated (VS-23)
Cross-references: - links to VS-08 (POS), VS-32 (returns), VS-23 (LP), VS-34 (reorder), VS-04 (DC pool), W4497 (EAS ops)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tag-leakage risk**: Reusable tags not returned to pool → shrink signal + replenishment cost; mitigated by shift pool reconciliation
- **Undetached-sale risk**: Tag not deactivated → exit alarm & customer friction; mitigated by detach-before-bag SOP
System Touchpoints: - POS detach (VS-08); returns (VS-32); LP/shrink (VS-23); procurement reorder (VS-34); DC tag pool (VS-04)
Time Estimate: - ~10–20 sec/sale detach; per-shift pool count ~10 min

steps.activity: Cashier detach/deactivate EAS hard-tags at paid sale (VS-08) using the detacher, and return reusable tags to the pool; soft-labels are deactivated
Returns (VS-32) re-apply tags to returned high-value items before restock, and reconcile tag pool counts (expected vs on-hand) per shift
LP/Auto-ID Lead investigate tag-pool shortages (lost/stolen tags = shrink/fraud signal), reorder pool stock (VS-34), and report shrink impact (VS-23)

fields.Participants: LP Officers, Store Manager, Legal (VS-100.3), Security (VS-98)

workflows.name: EAS Exception Response, Detention & Investigation Handoff

Automation Opportunity: - Alarm+CCTV+receipt correlation; case-management handoff to LP investigation (VS-23); wrongful-stop risk analytics
Controls: - CTL-685 (ensure controlled execution — EAS/RFID Tagging, Source-Tagging & Loss-Prevention Integration (PA-151.3).)
- CTL-685: verify-receipt-first SOP; lawful-procedure for detention; CCTV-documented; ORC escalation (VS-23)
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP/ORC), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-98 (security), VS-14.3 (PR/reputation), W4497 (EAS alert)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wrongful-detention risk**: False stop → customer harm, legal/PR exposure (VS-100.3/VS-14.3); mitigated by verify-receipt-first SOP & dignity standard
- **Evidence-gap risk**: Weak evidence → failed prosecution; mitigated by CCTV sync (VS-23) & documented procedure
System Touchpoints: - LP/ORC investigation (VS-23); legal/litigation (VS-100.3); security/contingent (VS-98); EAS alert (W4497)
Time Estimate: - ~5–15 min per alarm; confirmed cases hours+

steps.activity: LP/Stores respond to EAS alarms per SOP (approach, verify receipt, re-scan), balancing loss prevention with customer dignity and avoiding false detention (legal risk VS-100.3)
LP detains/interviews only on confirmed concealment with evidence, following lawful-procedure (DOLE/legal), and escalates to police/charges where warranted (links to VS-23 W840 ORC)
LP documents the incident, feeds organized/serial cases to ORC investigation (VS-23 W840/W1542), and reports to Legal (VS-100.3) for prosecution/civil recovery

fields.Trigger: System integration; analytics need; data-quality issue
fields.Volume: Auto-ID event stream (scans, EAS, RFID reads) → LP/inventory analytics

workflows.name: Auto-ID Data Integration to Loss-Prevention & Inventory Systems

Automation Opportunity: - Event-stream auto-correlation; LP exception-pattern ML (VS-125/VS-28); data-quality dashboards
Controls: - CTL-685 (ensure controlled execution — EAS/RFID Tagging, Source-Tagging & Loss-Prevention Integration (PA-151.3).)
- CTL-685: event architecture EA-governed (VS-113); data secured (VS-27.3) & retained per policy (VS-88); privacy-respecting (VS-91)
Cross-references: - links to VS-28/VS-27 (data/IT), VS-113 (EA), VS-23 (LP), VS-05 (inventory), VS-27.3/VS-88/VS-91 (security/retention/privacy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-gap risk**: Events not captured → blind LP analytics; mitigated by event-completeness monitoring
- **Privacy risk**: Auto-ID event data on customers/shoppers; mitigated by security (VS-27.3) & retention limits (VS-88/VS-91)
System Touchpoints: - IT/data platform (VS-28/VS-27); EA (VS-113); LP analytics (VS-23); inventory (VS-05); security (VS-27.3); retention (VS-88)

steps.activity: IT/EA/Auto-ID Lead design the auto-ID event architecture (POS scans, EAS exceptions, RFID reads → event stream → LP & inventory systems), per EA standards (VS-113) and data platform (VS-28)
Data/IT build LP analytics (exception patterns, scan-fail hotspots, tag-leakage) and inventory analytics (RFID count accuracy, phantom reads) on the platform (VS-28)
Auto-ID Lead/LP govern data quality (event completeness, latency), security (VS-27.3), and retention (VS-88) of auto-ID event data

fields.Trigger: Periodic review; program ROI; shrink trend
fields.Volume: EAS/RFID/tagging performance vs shrink (< 1.5% target) enterprise-wide

Automation Opportunity: - Automated tag-ROI/shrink-correlation model; under-protection auto-flag; shrink-vs-spend dashboard
Controls: - CTL-685 (ensure controlled execution — EAS/RFID Tagging, Source-Tagging & Loss-Prevention Integration (PA-151.3).)
- CTL-685: tagging ROI measured against shrink outcome (< 1.5%); policy tuned on data (W4484); spend governed (VS-135)
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP/shrink), VS-28 (BI), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-17.4/VS-135 (finance/TBM), W4484 (tagging policy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **ROI-blindness risk**: Tagging spend without shrink-correlation → wasted cost; mitigated by tag-ROI analytics
- **Metric-gaming risk**: Catch-rate up but shrink unchanged → measuring activity not outcome; mitigated by shrink-outcome linkage
System Touchpoints: - LP/shrink (VS-23); BI (VS-28); revenue assurance (VS-118); finance (VS-17.4); TBM (VS-135)

steps.activity: LP/BI measure EAS/RFID performance (catch rate, false-alarm rate, tag coverage, read accuracy) and tag-ROI (shrink reduction vs tagging cost) by category/store
LP/Merchandising correlate tagging coverage with shrink outcomes (VS-23/W840), identify under-protected categories, and tune the W4484 tagging policy
Finance/LP report shrink impact vs the < 1.5% target (profile §12.3) and tagging spend (links to VS-17.4/VS-135), driving investment decisions

fields.Volume: Auto-ID fraud-vector control (counterfeit labels, cloned barcodes, tag-switch) enterprise-wide

Automation Opportunity: - Anti-clone/2D-signature validation at POS; return-label match automation; EAS-defeat detection analytics
Controls: - CTL-685: anti-counterfeit labeling (VS-71); price-switch fraud controls (VS-23/VS-118); RFID privacy respected (VS-91); practices audited (VS-21)
Cross-references: - links to VS-23/VS-125 (LP/fraud), VS-71 (anti-counterfeit), VS-117 (PS/ICC), VS-32 (returns), VS-91 (privacy), VS-08.3 (override), VS-21 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Price-switch-fraud risk**: Cloned barcode → low-price scan on high-value item (VS-23/VS-118); mitigated by anti-clone codes & override audit (VS-08.3)
- **Privacy risk**: RFID tracking of customers; mitigated by tag-deactivation at sale & data minimization (VS-91)
System Touchpoints: - LP/fraud (VS-23/VS-125); anti-counterfeit (VS-71); compliance (VS-22); privacy (VS-91); IT security (VS-27.3); audit (VS-21)

steps.activity: LP/Fraud/Auto-ID Lead identify auto-ID fraud vectors (cloned/counterfeit barcodes for price-switching, fake PS/ICC labels VS-117, RFID/EAS defeat, label-swap at return VS-32) and design countermeasures
LP/Auto-ID Lead deploy countermeasures (anti-clone 2D codes, tamper-evident tags, return-receipt label match, EAS-defeat detection) and coordinate with Anti-Counterfeit (VS-71)

steps.a: VP Legal / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Compliance/Privacy/Audit ensure auto-ID practices respect data privacy (RFID/EAS event data on shoppers VS-91) and are audited (VS-21), with incident response (VS-23/VS-125)
